chunks: Jaʿfar sold, among those whom he sold, a Jaʿfarī female child who had been in the house and whom they had been raising. Then one of the ʿAlawīs was sent and informed the buyer of her situation, so the buyer said: “I am content to return her, provided that I not be deprived of anything from her price; so take her.” Then the ʿAlawī went and informed the people of the district of the matter, and they sent to the buyer forty-one dinars and instructed him to hand her over to her owner.

key_terms.الدَّارِ: the house or household in which she was being raised
key_terms.الْعَلَوِيِّينَ: one of the descendants of ʿAlī or a member of the ʿAlawī family
key_terms.الْمُشْتَرِيَ: the purchaser or buyer in the transaction
key_terms.ثَمَنِهَا: her price, meaning the amount paid for her
key_terms.جَعْفَرِيَّةً: a girl identified as belonging to the Jaʿfarī line or household

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe the return of a Jaʿfarī girl who had been sold?
ai.summary: This report narrates that a Jaʿfarī girl, who had been raised in the household, was sold by Jaʿfar. When her case was made known to the buyer, he agreed to return her on the condition that he not lose the purchase price, and the people of the district sent payment so that she could be restored to her owner. The narration reflects communal intervention in protecting rightful ownership and the interests of a vulnerable child.

en.hubeali: ‘Ja’far (brother of the 12<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) sold a Ja’farite female child among what he sold, who was in the house being nourished (by the 12<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>). So one of the Alawites went to the buyer informing of her news, and the buyer said, ‘I have made good with myself to return her, if I could get something from her price’. So the Alawite went and informed the people of the hand (of the 12<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup> of the news, and they sent to the buyer one hundred and forty Dinars and instructed him with handing her over to her guardian’.
en.sarwar: 28. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Muhammad ibn Harun ibn ‘Imran al-Hamadani who has said the following.

“I owed five hundred Dinars to the holy location (office of Imam al-Mahdi (a.s.). I felt extremely depressed about it. I said to myself, “The stores that have bought was for five hundred thirty Dinars. I will set them aside for the holy location (office of Imam al-Mahdi (a.s.).” However I had not said anything in words. He wrote to Muhammad ibn Ja‘far, “Take possession of the stores from Muhammad ibn Harun as payment for the five hundred Dinars that he owed us.”
